episode.title: Add a persistent policy for handing clicked links to the system browser
episode.before: At first parent 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40, an ordinary HTTP(S) click handled by ExternalLink reached openLink and opened an in-app preview. The system browser was selected only for an explicit native request, the platform open-elsewhere modifier or middle click, connector authorization links, HUD links, and non-HTTP(S) schemes. There was no stored user preference or settings control that changed the ordinary-click destination.
episode.after: At pinned merge 074349fb2744eacafbf80234444541aa736b1689, the desktop renderer owns an off-by-default, localStorage-backed boolean preference synchronized across open windows. A localized settings toggle changes that preference. The central clicked-link dispatcher consults it and, when enabled, sends normalized links through the existing operating-system browser bridge without creating an in-app preview. When disabled, prior routing remains intact. Explicit context-menu actions continue to invoke in-app preview or external handoff directly and are not overridden by the ordinary-click preference.
episode.diff: Relative to first parent 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40, the merge changes 9 desktop files with 101 insertions and 1 deletion: it adds the preference store and its persistence/cross-window tests; adds a settings toggle plus typed English, Russian, and Chinese copy; imports the preference into the central link dispatcher and adds it to the external-handoff guard; and adds a component test proving that an enabled preference sends a plain web-link click externally and leaves the preview collection empty.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned ref 074349fb2744eacafbf80234444541aa736b1689 is the merge of PR #120790, titled as a desktop setting to always open links in the external browser; its first parent is 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40.

The first-parent change comprises 9 desktop files, 101 insertions, and 1 deletion, including a new preference store, store tests, routing integration, routing tests, settings UI, and localization entries.

The new renderer-owned preference defaults to false, is stored under hermes.desktop.alwaysExternalLinks.v1, persists every atom update, and reacts to matching browser storage events so other open windows adopt the stored value.
Store tests assert the preference defaults off, persists both true and false transitions, and follows a matching storage event from another window.
The configuration settings surface subscribes to the preference and renders a ToggleRow whose change handler updates it.
The translation contract and English, Russian, and Chinese locales add a title and description explaining both ordinary-click external routing and the continuing explicit in-app-browser command.

The central openLink decision now reads the preference after URL normalization and before the existing authorization, HUD, and scheme guards; a true value selects openExternalLink, while a false value leaves the existing preview branch reachable.

ExternalLink intercepts ordinary anchor clicks, preserves consumer cancellation, derives an explicit native request from the component flag or modifier keys, and delegates the final destination decision to openLink.
In the first-parent version, the openLink external-routing guard did not consult any stored preference, so a normal HTTP(S) click fell through to the lazy in-app preview branch.

The pre-existing routing test establishes the baseline contract: a plain web-link click does not call the external bridge and instead creates an in-app preview; a modifier click calls the external bridge and creates no preview.
The added routing test enables the preference, performs a plain click, expects the operating-system bridge to receive the normalized URL, and expects the preview collection to remain empty.
Explicit context-menu choices bypass ordinary-click routing: Open in in-app browser calls openPreview directly, while Open in external browser calls openExternalLink directly.
Context-menu tests assert that both explicit destinations are offered for an ordinary chat link and that selecting Open in in-app browser creates a preview for the selected URL.
The desktop package declares Vitest as its test runner and exposes test and test:ui scripts suitable for executing the inspected store and component tests.

candidate_atomics.name: maintain_device_local_link_handoff_preference
candidate_atomics.title: Maintain a synchronized device-local link handoff preference
candidate_atomics.description: Represent the ordinary-click destination policy as an off-by-default renderer preference, persist changes locally, and reconcile matching storage events across open windows.

semantic_action.intent: Let a user's link destination choice survive subsequent clicks and remain consistent across concurrently open application windows.
semantic_action.pre_state: No stored boolean controls the ordinary-click browser destination, and separate renderer windows have no shared update signal for such a choice.
semantic_action.post_state: A boolean policy defaults to disabled, persists each update under a versioned local key, and converges to the stored value after another window emits a matching storage event.
semantic_action.validation: Assert the initial false value, persisted true and false transitions, and adoption of a true value after a matching StorageEvent.

candidate_atomics.name: expose_link_handoff_policy_control
candidate_atomics.title: Expose the link handoff policy as a localized settings control
candidate_atomics.description: Bind a user-facing toggle to the shared preference and describe the affected click behavior and preserved explicit override.

semantic_action.intent: Allow users to discover and change the ordinary-click destination policy without editing storage or configuration internals.
semantic_action.pre_state: The renderer may own a destination preference, but users have no typed, localized control for reading or changing it.
semantic_action.post_state: The settings screen reflects the current value and sends toggle changes to the preference owner, with locale contracts explaining the behavior and explicit in-app override.
semantic_action.validation: Type-check the translation contract and locale implementations, then render the settings surface and verify the toggle reads the current value and invokes the preference setter on change.

candidate_atomics.name: apply_link_handoff_policy_at_click_boundary
candidate_atomics.title: Apply the handoff policy at the central clicked-link boundary
candidate_atomics.description: Consult the preference in the shared click dispatcher so enabled ordinary clicks use the external browser while disabled behavior and explicit destination commands remain intact.

semantic_action.intent: Route every ordinary clicked link to the system browser when the user opts in, without regressing the default in-app path or explicit destination commands.
semantic_action.pre_state: A normalized HTTP(S) ordinary click opens an in-app preview unless another existing native-routing condition applies.
semantic_action.post_state: An enabled policy is an additional external-routing condition; a disabled policy preserves prior routing, and explicit context-menu actions continue to choose their destination directly.
semantic_action.validation: With the policy enabled, plain-click a web link and assert one external bridge call with no preview; with it disabled, retain the baseline plain-click preview and modifier-click external behavior; verify the explicit in-app context action still creates a preview.

candidate_workflows.name: add_user_selectable_link_browser_handoff
candidate_workflows.title: Add a user-selectable browser handoff policy for clicked links
candidate_workflows.description: Introduce a persistent destination policy, make it configurable, and enforce it at the common click boundary while preserving existing defaults and explicit destination choices.

workflow_graph.goal: Let users opt into sending ordinary application link clicks to the system browser while keeping the prior in-app default and explicit per-action destination controls.
when_to_use: A desktop or embedded application centrally intercepts link clicks and users need a persistent choice between an internal browser surface and the operating-system browser.
The application already has distinct internal-preview and external-handoff primitives that can remain authoritative for explicit actions.
anti_goals: Do not change the default destination for users who have not enabled the preference.
Do not replace or remove existing modifier, middle-click, authorization, special-surface, or non-web-scheme routing rules.
Do not make explicit Open in in-app browser or Open in external browser commands obey the ordinary-click preference.
Do not synchronize this device-specific UI preference through remote agent configuration.
not_applicable_when: Links are not intercepted by a common application-owned click dispatcher.
The application has no internal browser or preview destination to choose between.
Security or protocol policy requires a fixed destination that users must not override.
inputs: Behavioral tests for default, external, and explicit-override paths
workflow_graph.entry_state: Ordinary HTTP(S) clicks use the internal preview by default, external handoff is available only through existing special conditions or explicit commands, and no persistent user policy selects external handoff for every ordinary click.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The off-by-default policy persists locally and synchronizes across windows, is editable through localized settings, and causes enabled ordinary clicks to use the external bridge without creating previews while disabled and explicit-command behavior remains intact.

steps.condition: A destination choice must survive renderer lifetime and be visible to every open application window.
steps.validation: Run the store tests proving the false default, persistence in both directions, and reconciliation after a matching storage event.

steps.condition: Users need an application-supported way to inspect and change the policy.
steps.validation: Type-check locale completeness and verify the settings toggle is bound to the shared value and setter.

steps.condition: The common dispatcher can select between established internal-preview and external-handoff operations.
steps.validation: Run the link and context-menu tests covering enabled plain clicks, disabled baseline routing, modifier routing, absence of unwanted previews, and the explicit in-app command.

validation_ladder: Store-level: verify default value, durable true/false writes, and cross-window event reconciliation.
Dispatcher-level: verify enabled ordinary clicks call the external bridge and create no internal preview.
Regression-level: verify disabled ordinary clicks still open internally and modifier clicks still open externally.
Override-level: verify explicit context-menu destinations remain available and the in-app action still opens a preview.
Integration-level: run the desktop typecheck and Vitest UI suite declared by the pinned package.
stop_conditions: Stop if there is no single application-owned boundary through which ordinary clicks can consistently enforce the policy.
Stop if external handoff cannot be distinguished from internal preview in a behavioral oracle.
Stop if adding the preference would override mandatory protocol or security routing.
Stop if the prior default and explicit destination commands cannot be preserved and tested.
unresolved_or_deferred: The GitHub bundle does not include the PR body, review discussion, timeline, or status-check results.
The inspected tests provide direct behavioral oracles, but no fresh test execution result was available from the sparse repository checkout.

unresolved_questions: Were the pinned commit's desktop Vitest and typecheck jobs executed successfully in CI? The supplied GitHub evidence bundle marks status checks as unavailable.

Was persistence intentionally limited to browser localStorage across all supported desktop profiles? The implementation and comments establish device-local renderer ownership, but unavailable PR discussion prevents confirming broader product rationale.
